newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian farmers remove blocade after Prodi pledge.
newsitem.headline: Italian farmers remove blocade after Prodi pledge.

text.p: Italian farmers, demonstrating against European Union milk quotas, lifted a four-day blockade of roads leading to Milan's main airport on Monday after Prime Minister Romano Prodi promised to hear their grievances.
Prodi said in a statement he would meet a delegation on Wednesday provided roads to Linate airport were cleared and traffic allowed to move freely around Italy's second city.
"We will lift the blockade as a gesture of goodwill," one farmer said after Prodi set a date for the meeting.

Farmers descended on Milan last week in hundreds of tractors to protest against EU fines totalling 370 billion lire ($235 million) which were slapped on the Italian dairy industry for milk overproduction in the 1995-96 season.
The demonstrators have called on the state to pay the levies, due to be paid by January 31, and have demanded that the EU milk quotas be raised.
Prodi told reporters on Saturday that the government would give financial aid to the farmers in the form of soft loans but could not pay their fines.
The farmers' protest has brought chaos to road traffic around Linate, with air passengers forced to walk kilometres (miles) to catch their flights.

Farmers complain that they have fallen victim to tough EU quotas, introduced in the 1980s, which allow them to produce under 60 percent of Italy's milk needs. The rest of the milk is imported from other EU countries.
Last year Italian farmers produced 9.9 million tonnes of milk against 15 million tonnes consumed on the domestic market.

"Italy will ask the European Commission to increase that quota by 600,000 tonnes," Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto told reporters on Monday as he headed off for a meeting with the Commission in Brussels.
